qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507.mistake: The FOL statement FOL: ∀x ((¬p_13(x) ∧ ¬p_14(x)) ∨ p_15(x)) is not correctly corresponding to the NL: For all x, either x does not have attention to detail and x does not follow recipes, or x makes delicious drinks. The issue is with the logical structure. The FOL statement is of the form ∀x ((¬p₁₃(x) ∧ ¬p₁₄(x)) ∨ p₁₅(x)), which means for every x, either both (x lacks attention to detail AND doesn't follow recipes), OR x makes delicious drinks. But the natural language statement suggests that if x lacks attention to detail and doesn't follow recipes, then x doesn't make delicious drinks, or something like a conditional. However, the real problem is that the FOL is asserting a disjunction that is always true if p₁₅(x) is true, regardless of p₁₃ or p₁₄. But more importantly, the bracketing makes it (A ∧ B ∨ C), which is not equivalent to the likely intended meaning. It should have been ∀x (p₁₅(x) → (p₁₃(x) ∨ p₁₄(x))) or similar, to match “making delicious drinks requires attention to detail or following recipes”. But as is, the FOL does not correctly represent a meaningful interpretation of the NL, especially because it allows someone who makes delicious drinks without any conditions. The NL is best interpreted as implying that making delicious drinks requires one of the two, but the FOL says: either you lack both skills, OR you make delicious drinks — which is logically off. So the mapping is incorrect. Hence: False.
